attempts.text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"The corporate model of health care is inefficient, creates barriers to access and produces unnecessary deaths.", "claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"In 2008, the U.S. spent $2.2 trillion on health care, which was 16 percent of the U.S. gross domestic product.", "claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Consumer Reports estimates that one-quarter of U.S. health care spending in 2008 was wasted.", "claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Duplication of administrative bureaucracies is the largest source of waste in U.S. health care spending.", "claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"There are 1500 private health insurance companies in the U.S., each with its own administrative staff and paperwork.", "claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Three quarters of health care expenditures in the U.S. are consumed by the 10 percent of the population with chronic illnesses.", "claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Health insurance companies have a strong incentive to exclude people with chronic illnesses from their plans.", "claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"If health insurance companies exclude people with chronic illnesses from their plans, they can improve their margins while simultaneously offering lower premiums to their healthy customers.", "claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Institute of Medicine estimates that 45,000 people die each year due to lack of health insurance.", "claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The U.S. market-driven model of health care is responsible for the high cost of care in the U.S.", "claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[2]},],"unresolved_references":[]}
